subject: Renewal health + regional burst capacity / seat uplift proposal
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@brightcart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal health + regional burst capacity / seat uplift proposal

Hi Liam —

Quick summary from our renewal health check (attached): BrightCart's token consumption is up 48% QoQ driven by new personalization workflows in EU regions. Latency is within SLA for baseline traffic, but we see peak degradation on EU evenings that correlates with the personalization batch window.

Recommendation: two-part approach to keep unit economics strong while protecting UX during spikes:
- Temporary regional burst capacity (12-week window) to cover 2.5x peak (sits on Dedicated pool in EU)
- Seat uplift: convert 250k token/month from on-demand to a committed seat tier (saves ~22% per-token)

Estimated impact (attached calc): net cost per 1M tokens drops by ~16% after seat uplift; combined with burst capacity we avoid estimated ~2.2% conversion loss on peak hours.

Attachments: brightcart_q1_usage_summary.csv (CSV), regional_latency_report.pdf (PDF), proposed_term_amendment_draft.docx (DOCX - draft)

Ask: can we schedule a 30-min ops + procurement sync next week to align on thresholds and amendment language? If helpful I can include a short ROI slide.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Growth — Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: Renewal health + regional burst capacity / seat uplift proposal

Jonas —

Thanks for the note and the detailed packets. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering here:
1) Can you break down the 22% per-token savings into gross vs net after burst charges? We need an apples-to-apples number for procurement.
2) What's the SLA delta if we introduce burst capacity (any risk to baseline latency)?
3) We're evaluating contract language for a short-term burst addendum — procurement prefers a fixed not-to-exceed spend cap for the 12-week window.

Also looping in procurement@brightcart.com for availability next week.

—Liam
Head of Product Ops, BrightCart
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@brightcart.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health + regional burst capacity / seat uplift proposal

Liam — thanks, good questions. Short answers up front, details below and attached updated calc sheet.

1) Savings breakout: gross seat discount = 22% off on-demand list unit. After modeling expected burst utilization (we assume 15% of uplifted traffic hits burst in peak weeks) the realized net savings on the uplifted bucket is ~14% vs 100% on-demand. I've attached a per-week sensitivity table.

2) SLA delta: baseline latency SLOs remain unchanged. Burst runs on Dedicated capacity via the same runtime; it's configured to serve excess traffic with a soft-priority routing policy. During bursts the observed tail latency increases ~8–12ms in our tests, but we keep 99th percentile within contracted window. We can tighten routing to reduce tail at marginally higher cost.

3) Not-to-exceed cap: agreed — we propose a simple cap equal to 1.2x the projected incremental spend for the 12-week window (gives a ~20% safety margin). We can put this as an amendment line item with a spend-capture threshold to trigger notifications and automatic throttling.

Action items: Kimberly — can you confirm pricing language and the draft amendment flow? Markus — can ops validate the routing profile and confirm expected tail numbers for the EU cluster next Tuesday.

Best,
Jonas
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@brightcart.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health + regional burst capacity / seat uplift proposal

Hi all —

Pricing note: we can formalize the seat uplift as a committed tier for a 12-month term with an initial 12-week accelerated burst window. If BrightCart commits to the 250k token/month uplift for 12 months, the customer invoice model will show: committed discount (22%) applied to the uplift bucket, burst usage billed at the committed per-token rate up to the NTE cap; any consumption beyond NTE cap billed at on-demand.

I can draft amendment language that includes: NTE cap value, burst window dates, throttling/notification thresholds, and a rollback clause if average daily uplift falls under 50% of committed uplift for two consecutive weeks.

I'll attach the draft amendment docx and mark the procurement-facing sections.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@brightcart.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:42:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Renewal health + regional burst capacity / seat uplift proposal

Liam / BrightCart team —

Ops confirmation: EU cluster can support the 2.5x peak burst with the planned Dedicated configuration. Expected tail latency during simulated peak with soft-priority routing: +9ms median, +11ms 99th (within your current 99th contractual window). We'll enable KV prefix caching for personalization models which reduces backpressure and should trim peak CPU by ~18%.

I'll schedule a short deployment readiness run on Mon 29 Mar to exercise the routing and the billing meter boundaries. Jonas — I've attached the test plan as a short checklist.

Markus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
